requirement: Duplicate handling follows explicit hit/count semantics

inputs.name: default
inputs.call: check.py -> real gd-tools coverage merge run_a.json run_a.json (the identical file passed twice) (gd-tools-cli 0.4.0)

measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.finding: Merging identical input twice silently doubles the hit count (3 -> 6), with no duplicate-input detection, warning, or deduplication at any level -- not by file content, not by any run-identity concept (gd-tools' coverage-data format has no run ID field to key off of in the first place). gd-tools' merge treats every input positionally as an independent run to sum, full stop. A caller that (accidentally or via a retry/re-submission bug) passes the same run's output twice gets silently inflated counts with no diagnostic of any kind.

notes: This is a genuine negative finding, not a null result: the catalog's requirement asks for an EXPLICIT duplicate-handling policy, and gd-tools 0.4.0 has none -- its actual policy is 'sum everything, unconditionally,' which happens to be internally consistent (same rule as F070/F071) but provides no protection against or even awareness of duplicate input. This compounds with F069's finding (stale reports satisfy fresh checks with no warning): a CI pipeline that re-runs a failed upload step and ends up merging the same coverage file twice would see inflated-but-plausible-looking numbers with no error anywhere in the chain.

reviewer: independent review agent (fable), 2026-09-19: re-hashed run_a.json and check.py; re-ran check.py against the real merge CLI (3/3 pass: 3 -> 6, no warning). The negative finding reproduces exactly; nothing to correct.
ambiguities: Only byte-identical duplicate files are tested (the same file path passed twice). A 'duplicate run' in the more interesting sense -- two DIFFERENT coverage-data files that both happen to represent the same underlying test execution (e.g. re-exported twice) -- is not distinguishable from a genuinely independent second run using gd-tools' current coverage-data format at all, since it carries no run-identity field; this fixture cannot test a distinction the format itself doesn't support.
